messages:
hana: quick sync: proposal to add a "stress-sample" pass to onboarding. idea: pick a tiny set of adversarial-ish requests that historically flip e2e behaviors.
leo: sounds useful. how do we pick the stress samples without biasing model selection?
hana: selector rules: 1) pick examples with high regression-history score, 2) include 1 long-tail high-seqlen case, 3) include 1 short aggressive prompt. always seed with manifest.run_id for reproducibility.
bench-bot: (automated) note: stress-sample must be snapshotted and stored with run artifacts for postmortem.
tori: admission semantics? block on stress-sample fail or warn?
hana: plan: stress-sample failures surface as immediate P1 warnings for oncall; they do not block admission unless canonical shard also fails. we don't want the noise to block small dev rollouts.
leo: ok but for prod tiers we should escalate: stress-sample + any delta > threshold => block. we can map that to intake tier.
ops-bot: (automated) ops note: keep the stress-sample set capped to 5 examples per model to limit cost. also ensure replayability by capturing RNG seed.
tori: implementation: (1) selector service returns seeded list, (2) bench-runner snapshots them, (3) alerts hook maps hits to run id + examples for triage.
hana: i'll draft a tiny RFC and add a checklist item in intake-contrib: "stress-sample: seed, snapshot, tiered-action". target spike next week.
leo: thanks. if this reduces surprise-prod-flips it's worth the ops cost. demo please when you have a prototype.
